title: feat: publish hosted MCP servers to the official MCP registry
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #15529

- Generates hosted MCP listings from the existing shared registry, including the required Bearer API-key template.
- Adds a manual, main-only publishing workflow with an explicit version and GitHub OIDC; validates every entry before publishing any.
- Runs directly on Node 24 without a dependency install or a second publishing pipeline.
- Documents Smithery header forwarding and Glama/mcp.so submission and ownership steps in operations/mcp-registry/DIRECTORY_LISTINGS.md.

Validation: both focused tests pass; all six entries pass the official mcp-publisher v1.8.1 validator; actionlint and Biome pass. No registry login or publication performed. Directory submissions remain maintainer actions.

Maintainer follow-up incorporates the main-branch guard and official validation ideas from #15716, and ownership guidance from #15628. Contributors credited in the commit.

gist.headline: Six servers, one registry map
gist.blurb: The six hosted MCP servers now have listings ready for the official registry. Polli has labeled the shelves; a maintainer still has to open the shop.
gist.summary: Added a generator for six hosted MCP listings from the shared registry, including Bearer API-key templates, plus a manual main-branch workflow that validates every listing before publishing with GitHub OIDC.
gist.impact: Maintainers can validate and publish the six listings through a Node 24 workflow without installing dependencies; no registry publication has happened yet.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the official MCP registry as a cozy directory shelf holding six labeled server cards, with a key-shaped Bearer auth tag and a closed publishing gate. Polli checks the cards while a small CRT monitor robot holds the validation checklist; code-plants grow around the shelf. No external project mascot is indicated.
